place.zh: 沉鼎观 · 山门外的林子
place.en: Chending Temple · the woods outside the gate

setup.zh: 三试，胆子：林子里一只蠪侄，九首九尾，虎爪，叫声像婴儿，拴在古松上。一半的孩子哭着跑了。
setup.en: Third trial, nerve: in the woods a Longzhi — nine heads, nine tails, tiger claws, a cry like an infant's — chained to an old pine. Half the children run away crying.

recap.zh: 三试，胆子：你听出了蠪侄九个头里哪一个是真的；它扑来的那一刻，木牌一烫——「……左边」。
recap.en: Third trial, nerve: you heard which of the Longzhi's nine heads was real; as it lunged, the token burned — "…Left."

zh: 九首，九尾，虎爪；其音如婴儿。
锁链够不着的地方，站着一个人。
en: Nine heads, nine tails, tiger claws; a voice like an infant.
Just beyond the chain's reach, someone stands.

story.zh:
**三试 · 胆子。**

二试下来，剩了不到三百人。

三试考的地方，在山门外西边的一片老林子里。那林子里的树，一棵比一棵老，一棵比一棵黑，枝叶密得透不进一点天光，大白天走进去，也像走进了傍晚。林子正中是一棵古松，松树底下，拿一根比人腿还粗的铁链，拴着一只妖兽。

这妖兽叫作蠪侄。

它身子像狐狸，却比牛还大；九个脑袋，九条尾巴，四只爪子是虎的爪子。九个脑袋一齐转过来，盯着每一个走进林子的孩子；九张嘴一齐张开，叫起来，像九个婴儿在同时哭，哭声在林子里撞来撞去，撞得人头皮发麻，脚底发软。

执事站在林子口，道：「进去。走到古松底下，摸一下松树皮，出来。一个一个进。」

头一个进去的孩子，走了不到十步，便哭着跑了出来。第二个走了五步。第三个站在林子口，腿抖了半天，一步也没迈进去，给他爹从人群里拽走了。一个时辰下来，一小半的孩子，连林子的边都没敢进；进去了的，一大半是连滚带爬出来的。

马小宝进去了。

他走了三步。第三步落地的时候，蠪侄的九个脑袋一齐转向了他。马小宝站住了，一动不动，好一会儿，林子外头的人都瞧见，他那条绸裤子的裤腿底下，慢慢地洇开了一滩水。

两个家丁冲进林子，一左一右把他抬了出来。马小宝给抬在半空里，两条腿乱蹬，嘴里还在喊：「我没有！是露水！是露水！」

排队的时候，人堆里有个穿绸衫的孩子，正是早上在山门底下指着小满那张弓笑得前仰后合的那一个。他家里请过先生，读过几本书，这时候见大家都怕，便要显一显本事，清了清嗓子，摇头晃脑地背道：「又南五百里，曰凫丽之山……有兽焉，其状如狐，而九尾、九首、虎爪，名曰蠪侄，其音如婴儿——」

背到这里，他顿住了。

旁边一个孩子问：「其音如婴儿，然后呢？」

那穿绸衫的孩子脸色慢慢地白了，嘴唇哆嗦了两下，才把最后三个字挤出来：「……是、食、人。」

四下里登时一片死寂。过了一会儿，不知是谁先「哇」的一声哭了出来，跟着便哭成了一片。那穿绸衫的孩子自己哭得最响。

小满没有哭。他蹲在一边，把「是食人」三个字在心里过了一遍，想的却是：吃人。那它一定很饿。

轮到沈小满之前，他在林子外头等了将近一个时辰。

别的孩子等的时候，有的在哭，有的在跟爹娘说话，有的闭着眼睛念佛，有的蹲在地上抓了一把土往自己脸上抹，说是抹了土，妖怪便闻不出人味——这也是那卖登仙符的教的，另收五文。小满什么也没做。他就蹲在林子边上，歪着头，听。

他听了一个时辰。那九个脑袋叫一回，他听一回；叫一回，他听一回。听到后来，他发觉一桩怪事：每回那九张嘴一齐张开，九种哭声一齐涌出来，可林子深处那棵古松的松针，只跟着其中一种哭声抖。别的八种，哭得再响，松针一动也不动。

小满心里便有了数。可他没有说。他爹说过，看见了鹿，先别喊，喊了，鹿就跑了，旁人也就知道了。

轮到沈小满了。

他走进林子，没有往前冲，站在铁链够不着的地方，站定了。

九个脑袋一齐转过来，盯着他。九张嘴一齐张开，哭。

小满没有看那九个脑袋。

他是猎户家的孩子，从会走路起，就跟着他爹在山里听声音。他爹教过他：山里的声音，十样里有九样是骗人的。风钻过石缝，像狼嚎；水漫过枯枝，像人哭；空树洞里的回声，比真的熊还吓人。真的只有一样，真的那一样，是从一个活物的肚子里出来的，带着热气，带着那活物自己的饿。他爹说，你分不清的时候，就闭上眼睛。眼睛会骗你，耳朵不会。

小满便闭上了眼睛。

九种哭声，一齐涌进他耳朵里来。他一种一种地听。

第一种，是空的，像风灌进一只破瓦罐。第二种，也是空的，像有人对着一口枯井喊了一声，井底下应回来的那一声。第三种、第四种，空的。第五种，空的，空得像庙里的钟，敲过了，只剩一圈一圈的嗡嗡声。第六种、第七种，空的。第九种，空的。

只有第八种，不是。

第八种，是从胸腔里出来的。一呼一吸之间，带着热气，带着一股说不出的腥，还带着一点——小满后来想了很久，才想出一个词来——饿。那是一种很深很深的饿，饿得发慌，饿得不管不顾，好像把整座林子吃下去，把整座山吃下去，也不会饱。

另外八个，都是它的影子。

小满睁开眼睛，弯下腰，从地上捡起了一块石头。
story.en:
**Third trial · Nerve.**

After the second trial, fewer than three hundred were left.

The third trial was held in an old forest west of the mountain gate. Its trees were each older and darker than the last, the leaves so dense not a speck of sky came through; walk in at midday and it was like walking into dusk. At the forest's heart stood an ancient pine, and under the pine, chained by an iron chain thicker than a man's leg, was a demon beast.

It was called a Longzhi.

Its body was like a fox's, but bigger than an ox; nine heads, nine tails, and four tiger's paws. The nine heads all turned to stare at every child who walked into the forest; the nine mouths all opened, and when it cried it was like nine babies crying at once, the crying bouncing round the forest till your scalp crawled and your feet went soft.

A steward stood at the edge of the forest. "In you go. Walk to the old pine, touch the bark once, come out. One at a time."

The first child in went fewer than ten steps and ran out crying. The second went five. The third stood at the forest's edge, legs shaking, and didn't take one step before his father dragged him away through the crowd. In an hour, a good part of the children didn't dare go even to the edge; of those who went in, most came out crawling and rolling.

Ma Xiaobao went in.

He went three steps. As the third foot landed, the Longzhi's nine heads all turned toward him together. Ma Xiaobao stood still, not moving, for a good while, and everyone outside the forest saw a puddle slowly spread beneath the legs of his silk trousers.

Two servants rushed in and carried him out between them. Hoisted in mid-air, legs kicking, he was still shouting: "I didn't! It's dew! It's dew!"

While they queued, a boy in a silk gown in the crowd — the very one who'd pointed at Xiaoman's bow at the gate that morning and laughed himself double — seeing everyone afraid, wanted to show off his learning. His family had hired a tutor; he'd read a few books. He cleared his throat and recited, wagging his head: "Another five hundred li south is Mount Fuli… there is a beast there, shaped like a fox, with nine tails, nine heads and tiger's claws, named the Longzhi; its cry is like a baby's —"

There he stopped.

A child beside him asked: "Its cry is like a baby's — and then?"

The silk-gowned boy's face slowly went white; his lips trembled twice before he squeezed out the last three words: "…it — eats — people."

Dead silence all round. After a while, who knows who first went *waah*, and then it was crying everywhere. The silk-gowned boy cried loudest of all.

Xiaoman didn't cry. He crouched to one side and turned the three words *eats people* over in his head, and what he thought was: eats people. Then it must be very hungry.

Before Shen Xiaoman's turn he waited outside the forest nearly an hour.

While they waited other children cried, or talked to their parents, or shut their eyes and prayed, or crouched and rubbed a handful of earth on their faces — rub on earth, and the demon can't smell a person; this too the talisman seller taught, five coppers extra. Xiaoman did none of it. He just crouched at the forest's edge, head tilted, listening.

He listened an hour. Each time the nine heads cried, he listened; cried, listened. By the end he'd noticed something strange: every time the nine mouths opened together and nine kinds of crying poured out, the needles of the old pine deep in the forest trembled to only one of the cries. The other eight, however loud, didn't stir a needle.

Then Xiaoman knew. But he didn't say. His father had said: see the deer, don't shout; shout, and the deer runs, and everyone else knows.

It was Shen Xiaoman's turn.

He walked into the forest and didn't charge; he stopped where the chain couldn't reach, and stood.

The nine heads all turned and stared at him. The nine mouths all opened, and cried.

Xiaoman didn't look at the nine heads.

He was a hunter's boy; since he could walk he'd followed his father into the mountains listening to sounds. His father had taught him: of ten sounds in the mountains, nine lie. Wind through a crack in the rock sounds like a wolf's howl; water over dead branches sounds like a person crying; the echo in a hollow tree is scarier than a real bear. Only one is real, and the real one comes out of a living thing's belly, with heat in it, with that thing's own hunger. His father said: when you can't tell, shut your eyes. Eyes lie to you; ears don't.

So Xiaoman shut his eyes.

The nine kinds of crying poured into his ears together. He listened to them one by one.

The first was hollow, like wind blown into a broken jar. The second was hollow too, like someone calling into a dry well and the answer coming back up from the bottom. The third and fourth, hollow. The fifth hollow, hollow as a temple bell after it's struck, only the ring left humming round and round. The sixth and seventh, hollow. The ninth, hollow.

Only the eighth was not.

The eighth came out of a chest. Between one breath and the next it carried heat, an indescribable rankness, and a little — Xiaoman thought a long time afterwards before finding the word — hunger. A very, very deep hunger, frantic, reckless, as though eating the whole forest, the whole mountain, would never make it full.

The other eight were all its shadows.

Xiaoman opened his eyes, bent, and picked up a stone.

exits.means: fights the Longzhi, takes the third trial

withdrawn.zh: 蠪侄缩回古松后面，九个头龇着牙。瞿老：「再来。」
withdrawn.en: The Longzhi shrinks back behind the pine, nine heads baring their teeth. Elder Qu: "Again."

story.zh:
说时迟那时快，那蠪侄已扑了过来！铁链「哗啦」一声绷得笔直，古松都给扯得晃了一晃，一只虎爪带着风，劈头盖脸地朝他扫过来——便在这时，小满胸口那块木牌忽然一烫，烫得他心口一跳，一个很小、很困、像是从极深极深的地方浮上来的声音，在他耳朵里道：

⟪「……左边。」⟫

他想也没想，往右一滚。

那虎爪擦着他的左肩扫了过去，扫断了他身后一棵碗口粗的小松树，「咔嚓」一声，松树倒了，松针落了他一头一脸。小满趴在地上，心里想：你爷爷的，九个脑袋。

他手里那块石头，却已经出手了。

石头不偏不倚，正正地砸在第八个脑袋的鼻尖上。

蠪侄登时愣住了。它那一扑的势子，在半空里停了一停，像是忽然忘了自己要做什么。然后，另外八个脑袋，一下子散了，像一阵烟，像一口哈在冬天窗户上的热气，眨一眨眼，便什么都没有了。林子里只剩下一只狐狸模样的兽，一个脑袋，一条尾巴，比牛还大，却捂着鼻子，委委屈屈地「呜」了一声，夹着尾巴，缩回古松后面去了。

林子里忽然很静。

小满从地上爬起来，拍了拍身上的松针。他回头一看，林子口拄着扫帚站着那个扫地的老头，也不知站了多久，看了多久。老头脸上什么神气也没有，只是那把扫帚，没有在扫。

小满摸了摸胸口的木牌。它又凉了，凉得像从来没有热过。

他小声道：「……谢了。」

木牌没有回答。

他又小声道：「……记账？」

木牌，轻轻地，暖了一下。

小满道：「对不住。砸疼了吧。」

那兽没作声，把捂着鼻子的爪子，放下来了一点点。它的鼻头，给石头砸得通红，红得像一根萝卜。

小满站起身，走出了林子。

这个听声的法子，沈小满这一辈子，后来又用过一回。那一回，也是九个头，也是八个空的，一个真的；那一回他闭着眼睛听了很久很久，听到最后，听出那个真的，是从哪里来的。那是许多许多年以后的事了。十三岁的沈小满站在林子里，头上顶着一头松针，只知道自己过了三试，饿得前胸贴后背。
story.en:
Quick as you like, the Longzhi sprang! The iron chain snapped taut with a *clank*, the old pine itself swayed, and a tiger's paw came sweeping at his head on a gust of wind — and just then the token at Xiaoman's chest suddenly burned, burned so his heart jumped, and a very small, very sleepy voice, as if surfacing from very, very deep down, said in his ear:

⟪"…Left."⟫

Without a thought he rolled right.

The paw swept past his left shoulder and snapped a pine as thick as a bowl behind him — *crack* — the pine came down and showered him head and face with needles. Xiaoman lay on the ground thinking: Your grandpa's — nine heads.

But the stone in his hand had already flown.

The stone struck, dead true, on the tip of the eighth head's nose.

The Longzhi froze. Its spring hung a moment in mid-air, as if it had suddenly forgotten what it meant to do. Then the other eight heads scattered all at once, like a puff of smoke, like breath on a winter window — blink, and there was nothing. In the forest there was only a fox-like beast, one head, one tail, bigger than an ox, clutching its nose, giving an aggrieved *whuu*, and slinking back behind the old pine with its tail between its legs.

The forest was suddenly very quiet.

Xiaoman got up off the ground and brushed off the needles. He looked back: at the forest's edge, leaning on his broom, stood the old sweeper — how long he'd stood, how long he'd watched, who knew. His face showed nothing; only the broom wasn't sweeping.

Xiaoman felt the token at his chest. It was cool again, cool as if it had never been warm.

He said softly: "…Thanks."

The token didn't answer.

He said softly again: "…It goes in the books?"

The token, gently, warmed once.

Xiaoman said, "Sorry. Did that hurt?"

The beast made no sound, but lowered the paws clutching its nose a tiny bit. Its nose, where the stone struck, was red — red as a radish.

Xiaoman stood and walked out of the forest.

This way of listening, Shen Xiaoman used once more in his life. That time too there were nine heads, eight hollow and one real; that time he listened with his eyes shut a long, long time, and at the end heard where the real one came from. That was many, many years later. Thirteen-year-old Shen Xiaoman, standing in the forest with pine needles in his hair, knew only that he'd passed the third trial, and was so hungry his belly touched his back.
